title: A Multi-Agent Framework for Stateful Inference-Time Search

mechanism.domainTask: Automated unit test generation and edge-case discovery
mechanism.populationDetail: A bounded flat archive of multiple edge-case candidates is retained across search stages; no islands or genealogy are maintained.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The algorithm retains the top-K edge cases ranked by reward across the accumulated candidates.
mechanism.replacementDetail: The archive update is an archive-level top-K survivor rule, while the controller also preserves full state history.
mechanism.generationDetail: The actor proposes new edge cases from source code and accumulated state; no specific parent candidate is directly edited.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Coverage, mutation, and exception signals are fed back into the persistent state and reward-guided archive update.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: none_explicit; evaluator metadata and prior edge cases are resurfaced

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/A Multi-Agent Framework for Stateful Inference-Time Search.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: The paper has no explicit parent candidate; archive/history entries are contextual state rather than true parent candidates. The paper is explicitly cited in the survey for flat multi-population, multi-elite archives, replacement, implicit exploration-exploitation, and evaluator-metadata-based selection. Prompt details are partly exposed in the appendix; model count is per-run rather than across the evaluation suite.
